podcast.title: Plagiarism Lawsuit Against John Fogarty (1985)
podcast.body: Saul Zaentz, who owned the copyrights to Credence Clearwater Revival's songs (including "Run Through the Jungle") through Fantasy Records, sued John Fogarty for plagiarism. Zaentz alleged that Fogarty's solo song "Old Man Down the Road" sounded too similar to "Run Through the Jungle," a song Zaentz owned the copyright to, despite Fogarty having written both. "While in Saul freaked out, got all bent out of shape, and then he sued John for plagiarism, alleging that a song on Center Field called Old Man Down the Road, which John owned, sounded just like an old CCR song called Run Through the Jungle, which Saul owned as the result of the contract dispute."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Antagonistic Relationship with John Fogarty
podcast.body: There was a lot of loathing between Saul Zaentz and John Fogarty, stemming from Fogarty's decision to give up ownership of his CCR songs to Zaentz to escape his contract with Fantasy Records. "There was a lot of loathing on both sides."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Plagiarism Lawsuit for Self-Plagiarism (1985)
xref.body: John Fogarty, founder and chief songwriter for Credence Clearwater Revival, was sued for plagiarism in 1985 after releasing his solo album "Center Field." The lawsuit alleged that songs on his solo album, specifically "Old Man Down the Road," stole melodies from old CCR songs like "Run Through the Jungle," the copyrights of which were owned by Saul Zaentz of Fantasy Records, not Fogarty himself. "Then, in 1985, John released a solo record called Center Field and it too did very, very well. But then John was served with a lawsuit alleging plagiarism."

xref.title: Contract Dispute and Copyright Transfer
xref.body: John Fogarty had given ownership of his Credence Clearwater Revival songs to Saul Zaentz, who ran CCR's record label, Fantasy Records, in order to get out of his contract, indicating a strong animosity between them. "Although John had written the songs for Credence, the copyrights, the ownership of the songs he had written, had been given over to a guy named Saul Zance."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Copyright Ownership Dispute
xref.body: The copyrights to songs written by John Fogarty for Credence Clearwater Revival were transferred to Saul Zaentz, who ran the band's record label, Fantasy Records, as part of a contract dispute settlement. This led to a bizarre lawsuit where Fogarty was sued for plagiarizing himself. "Although John had written the songs for Credence, the copyrights, the ownership of the songs he had written, had been given over to a guy named Saul Zance."
